hook: David Silver is a computer scientist known for leading reinforcement learning research at DeepMind. He earned his PhD at the University of Alberta under reinforcement learning pioneer Richard Sutton, then became a professor at University College London while also leading DeepMind's reinforcement learning research. He led the teams behind DeepMind's Atari-playing deep Q-network, AlphaGo, AlphaGo Zero, AlphaZero, and MuZero, a series of systems that mastered Go, chess, shogi, and Atari games through self-play and learned models. He later contributed to AlphaFold's protein structure predictions and to AlphaProof, a system that reached silver-medal-level performance at the International Mathematical Olympiad. He has since stepped back from leading DeepMind's reinforcement learning team to become CEO of a new venture, Ineffable Intelligence, while remaining a professor at UCL.
name: David Silver

quote.text: AI that learns for itself to solve problems that humans can't
quote.context: Description of his research mission on his personal website, davidstarsilver.wordpress.com

moniker: Reinforcement learning pioneer, lead of AlphaGo and MuZero

secondary.name: Mastering the game of Go with deep neural networks and tree search, Nature 2016

timeline.event: AlphaGo defeated world champion Lee Sedol
timeline.impact: First time an AI program beat a top professional Go player, a landmark result for deep reinforcement learning.

timeline.event: Published AlphaGo Zero, learning Go from self-play alone
timeline.impact: Removed the need for human game records, learning entirely from self-play.

timeline.event: Published AlphaZero, generalizing self-play mastery to chess and shogi
timeline.impact: Showed a single algorithm could reach superhuman play in multiple games from the rules alone.
Achieved superhuman play in Go, chess, shogi, and Atari without being given the rules of the environment.

timeline.event: Contributed to AlphaProof's International Mathematical Olympiad results
timeline.impact: Applied reinforcement learning and formal proof search to reach silver-medal-level performance on IMO problems.

quick_facts: PhD from the University of Alberta, advised by reinforcement learning pioneer Richard Sutton
Professor at University College London and former lead of DeepMind's reinforcement learning research
Led AlphaGo, AlphaGo Zero, AlphaZero, and MuZero, published in Nature and Science
Contributed to AlphaFold and to AlphaProof's International Mathematical Olympiad results
Fellow of the Royal Society and Fellow of AAAI
Recipient of the ACM Prize in Computing

achievements.title: Led AlphaGo
achievements.impact: Built the first program to defeat a professional Go player and, in 2016, the world champion Lee Sedol, a milestone many expected was a decade away.

achievements.title: Led AlphaGo Zero and AlphaZero
achievements.impact: Showed that a single algorithm could master Go, chess, and shogi purely through self-play, without any human game data.

achievements.title: Led MuZero
achievements.impact: Extended self-play mastery to settings where the rules of the environment are not known in advance, unifying planning and model-based learning.

achievements.title: ACM Prize in Computing
achievements.impact: Recognized for fundamental contributions to reinforcement learning and its application to superhuman game-playing systems.
